title: Talking about the past
intro: When Dutch people talk about yesterday or last weekend, they mostly use heb or ben plus a past form at the end. This lesson shows how to make those past forms, when to use ben, and the short past forms like was and had that you hear all the time.

notes.title: 1. The everyday past: heb + a ge- word at the end
body: Dutch talks about the past mostly with hebben. Put heb, hebt, heeft or hebben in second place. The past form of the main verb goes to the very end.
English “I played” becomes “I have played”: ik heb gespeeld. You use this form even when English uses the simple past.

examples.en: I played guitar.
We ate pancakes.
What did you do at school?

notes.title: 2. Regular verbs: ge + stem + d or t
body: For a regular verb, take the stem. That is the ik form: spelen gives speel, werken gives werk. Put ge- in front and -d or -t at the end.
If the stem ends in t, k, f, s, ch or p, add -t. These are the consonants in the phrase [’t kofschip]. Everything else gets -d. If the stem already ends in t or d, add nothing.
You can't hear the difference, because a final d sounds like a t. It matters only when you write.

examples.en: I worked at home. (werk ends in k)
She danced all afternoon. (dans ends in s)
I trained hard. (train ends in n)
I waited a long time. (wacht already ends in t)

links.label: Wikibooks Dutch, lesson 6: Past forms on -d and -t

notes.title: 3. Common irregular verbs, and verbs without ge-
body: Many everyday verbs have their own past form. Learn them as words: gegaan, gedaan, gezien, gegeten, gedronken, gekocht, gelopen, gezwommen.
Verbs that start with be-, ver-, ont-, her- or ge- get no extra ge-. Betalen becomes betaald, and vergeten stays vergeten.

examples.en: I bought a new guitar. (kopen)
Have you paid yet? (betalen)
I forgot my keys. (vergeten)

links.label: Wikibooks Dutch, lesson 6: Verbs without ge-

notes.title: 4. ben or heb? Going somewhere, or a change
body: Use zijn (ben, bent, is, zijn) when someone goes to a place, or when something changes. Common ones are gaan, komen, blijven, worden and beginnen.
Lopen, fietsen and zwemmen can take either. If you name the place you went to, use ben. If you only talk about the activity, use heb.

examples.nl: Ze [is] met de fiets naar school [gegaan].
examples.en: She went to school by bike.
I walked home.
I cycled for an hour.
She turned six in March.

links.label: Wikibooks Dutch, lesson 12: Verbs of motion with zijn or hebben
Wikibooks Dutch, lesson 12: Verbs that take zijn

notes.title: 5. Split verbs in the past: ge- goes in the middle
body: With split verbs like ophalen and meenemen, ge- goes between the two parts, and you write it as one word: opgehaald, meegenomen, opgestaan.

examples.nl: Ik heb haar om drie uur [opgehaald].
examples.en: I picked her up at three.
Did you bring your PE things?
What time did you get up?

notes.title: 6. Towards A2: was, had and other one-word past forms
body: For zijn and hebben, Dutch speakers use a one-word past all the time: was and waren, had and hadden.

Other verbs mostly use heb or ben when people talk. In stories and messages you also see one-word past forms. Regular verbs add -de or -te to the stem, with the same ’t kofschip rule: ik speelde, ik werkte. Irregular ones change: ging, kwam, zag.

examples.en: It was really nice.
We didn't have time.
I used to play in a band.

links.label: Wikibooks Dutch, lesson 6: Past tense with -de and -te

cards.rule: heb second, gespeeld at the end.

cards.nl: Wat heb je dit weekend gedaan?
cards.en: What did you do this weekend?

reply.nl: We zijn naar het strand gegaan.

cards.rule: Question word, heb, then gedaan at the end.
eten becomes gegeten. Learn it as a word.

cards.nl: Wat heb je op school gedaan?
cards.en: What did you do at school?
cards.rule: doen becomes gedaan.
werk ends in k, so add -t: gewerkt.

cards.nl: Ze heeft de hele middag gedanst.
cards.rule: dans ends in s, so add -t: gedanst.
train ends in n, so add -d: getraind.

cards.nl: Ik heb een nieuwe gitaar gekocht.
cards.rule: kopen becomes gekocht.
betalen starts with be-, so no extra ge-: betaald.
vergeten starts with ver-, so it stays vergeten.

cards.nl: Ze is met de fiets naar school gegaan.
cards.en: She went to school by bike.
cards.rule: Going to a place: is, not heeft.
You name the place you went to, so use ben.

cards.nl: Ik heb vandaag vijf kilometer gelopen.
alts: Vandaag heb ik vijf kilometer gelopen.
cards.rule: Only the activity, no place you went to, so use heb.

cards.nl: Ze is in maart zes geworden.
cards.rule: A change, with worden: is.

cards.en: What time did you get up?
cards.rule: opstaan becomes opgestaan, with ben.

cards.nl: Ik heb haar om drie uur opgehaald.
cards.en: I picked her up at three.
alts: Om drie uur heb ik haar opgehaald.
cards.rule: ophalen becomes opgehaald: ge- in the middle.

cards.en: Did you bring your PE things?
cards.rule: meenemen becomes meegenomen.
was: the one-word past of is.
hadden: the one-word past of hebben.
waren: the one-word past of zijn, for more than one person.
Question word, was, then the rest.

cards.nl: Vroeger speelde ik in een band.
cards.en: I used to play in a band.
alts: Ik speelde vroeger in een band.
cards.rule: One-word past: speel + de.
